subject: History
description: Aurangzeb (1658-1707) — Deccan campaigns, conflicts with Marathas, Bijapur, Golconda, religious policy, jizya, fall of Mughal empire.

questions.stem: AURANGZEB SPENT THE LAST 26 YEARS of his reign primarily campaigning in:
questions.explanation: AURANGZEB (r. 1658-1707) — last great Mughal emperor. The LAST 26 YEARS (1681-1707) were spent in the DECCAN, attempting to crush MARATHAS, conquer BIJAPUR & GOLCONDA. KEY CAMPAIGNS: (1) BIJAPUR — annexed 1686 (Adil Shahi dynasty extinguished). (2) GOLCONDA — annexed 1687 (Qutb Shahi dynasty extinguished); Aurangzeb captured the famous KOH-I-NOOR diamond and DECCAN GOLD here. (3) MARATHAS — eternal nemesis. Captured Sambhaji (Shivaji's son, 1689) and TORTURED him to death; but Maratha resistance only intensified under Rajaram, then Shahu. AURANGZEB DIED in 1707 in AHMADNAGAR, Deccan, age 88; never returned to Delhi. WHY DECCAN OBSESSION: (1) Religious — Sunni vs Shia (Bijapur, Golconda were Shia). (2) Strategic — Maratha raiders disrupted Mughal heartland. (3) Wealth — Deccan gold/diamonds. CONSEQUENCES: (1) MILITARY OVEREXTENSION — empire stretched thin. (2) HUGE FINANCIAL DRAIN — daily ~Rs 4 lakh on military. (3) PEASANT REVOLTS in north India (Sikhs, Jats, Satnamis). (4) MARATHAS NOT crushed — they regrouped post-1707, eventually became dominant power until 1818. AFTERMATH: 'AFTER AURANGZEB, THE DELUGE' — empire fragmented under weak successors; Mughal supremacy ended within 30 years. PYQ FREQUENCY: Aurangzeb-Deccan in UPSC, MPSC, SSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: AURANGZEB re-imposed JIZYA tax on which group in 1679?
questions.explanation: JIZYA — TAX on NON-MUSLIMS in Islamic states (in lieu of zakat which Muslims pay). Established in earlier Islamic kingdoms; ABOLISHED by AKBAR (1564). RE-IMPOSED by AURANGZEB on 2 APRIL 1679 — major break from Akbar's tolerant policy. RATES: rich paid 48 dirhams; middle class 24; poor 12. Brahmins, women, children, monks, disabled were exempt. WHY: Aurangzeb's ORTHODOX SUNNI ISLAMIC outlook + financial need (ongoing Deccan campaigns drained treasury). RESPONSE: PROTESTS — sit-ins by Hindu merchants in Delhi; widespread anger. RAJPUTS who had been Mughal allies (since Akbar's marriages) FELT BETRAYED — Mewar, Marwar (Jodhpur) rebellions. MARATHA ANGER fueled their revolt. SHIVAJI's son SAMBHAJI HARSHLY criticized Jizya. SIKHS — Guru Tegh Bahadur (9th Sikh Guru) was EXECUTED 1675 for protecting Kashmiri Pandits forced to convert; this preceded jizya but reflected same trend. ABOLITION: jizya was finally abolished by JAHANDAR SHAH (1712, briefly) and permanently by FARRUKHSIYAR (1717). AKBAR's POLICY: in Akbar's view, RULE OF LAW (suluh-i-kul, peace with all) ensured peasant cooperation, military strength via Rajput allies, prosperity. AURANGZEB reversed this — narrow religious base. RESULT: MUGHAL EMPIRE WEAKENED. PYQ FREQUENCY: jizya re-imposition in UPSC History optional, NCERT Class 12, MPSC.

questions.stem: Which Sikh Guru was executed by Aurangzeb in 1675 in Delhi?
questions.explanation: GURU TEGH BAHADUR (1621-1675) — the 9TH SIKH GURU. Executed by Aurangzeb in DELHI on 24 NOVEMBER 1675 at GURUDWARA SIS GANJ SAHIB (built later at the execution site, near Chandni Chowk). REASON: Hindu BRAHMINS of Kashmir came to Guru Tegh Bahadur seeking protection from forced conversion to Islam under Mughal pressure. The Guru went to Delhi to confront Aurangzeb; refused to convert; was beheaded. Title: 'HIND DI CHADAR' (Shield of India / Protector of Hindus). HIS SON GURU GOBIND SINGH became the 10th Guru and TRANSFORMED Sikhism — created the KHALSA on Vaisakhi 1699 (Anandpur Sahib), establishing the warrior-saint tradition; died 1708 at Nanded. SIKH GURUS sequence: (1) Nanak (founder, 1469-1539). (2) Angad (1539-52). (3) Amar Das (1552-74). (4) Ram Das (1574-81). (5) Arjan (1581-1606, compiled Adi Granth, executed by Jahangir). (6) Hargobind (1606-44, militarized). (7) Har Rai (1644-61). (8) Har Krishan (1661-64, child Guru). (9) TEGH BAHADUR (1664-75, executed by Aurangzeb). (10) Gobind Singh (1675-1708, founded Khalsa). After Guru Gobind Singh, the GURU GRANTH SAHIB (sacred scripture) became the eternal Guru. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sikh Gurus, Mughal-Sikh conflict in UPSC, MPSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Aurangzeb defeated and EXECUTED Shivaji's son SAMBHAJI in:
questions.explanation: SAMBHAJI MAHARAJ (1657-1689) — Chhatrapati of the Maratha Empire after Shivaji's death (1680). Captured by Mughal forces under MUQARRAB KHAN at SANGAMESHWAR (Maharashtra) on 1 February 1689 — betrayed by his brother-in-law GANOJI SHIRKE who informed Mughals of his location. TORTURE + EXECUTION: Aurangzeb ordered his eyes plucked out, tongue cut, then beheading on 11 March 1689 at TULAPUR (near Pune). REASON CITED: refused to convert to Islam, accept Mughal subsidiary status. LEGACY: Maratha resistance INTENSIFIED, not weakened. His brother RAJARAM took over (1689-1700); then his widow TARABAI (regent for son Shivaji II, 1700-1707); then Shahu (Sambhaji's son, who was Mughal hostage and released after Aurangzeb's death) — under Shahu, Marathas became the dominant Indian power until 1818. SAMBHAJI's SHRINE — at Tulapur, near Pune; visited by lakhs of Marathi devotees. SAMBHAJI's COURT INCLUDED: KAVI BHUSHAN — Hindi poet who composed verses praising Sambhaji's bravery. Sambhaji was an ACCOMPLISHED SANSKRIT SCHOLAR — wrote 'BUDH BHUSHANAM' (Sanskrit treatise on rajaniti). AURANGZEB and SAMBHAJI battles: 1681-89 — multiple skirmishes; Aurangzeb committed enormous resources but Marathas evaded full defeat. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sambhaji-Aurangzeb in UPSC, MPSC, SSC modern history 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Aurangzeb's annexation of GOLCONDA in 1687 brought him control over which famous diamond mines?
questions.explanation: GOLCONDA — capital of QUTB SHAHI dynasty (founded 1518); ruled Telangana region of southern India for nearly 170 years. MAJOR DIAMOND MINES: KOLLUR, PARITALA in present-day Andhra Pradesh — produced INDIA's most famous diamonds throughout history. WORLD-FAMOUS DIAMONDS from Golconda mines: (1) KOH-I-NOOR — 'Mountain of Light'; original ~793 carats, recut to 105 carats; through Mughals → Nadir Shah (1739) → Ahmad Shah Abdali → Maharaja Ranjit Singh → British (1849). Now in Queen Mother's crown (UK). (2) HOPE DIAMOND — blue 45.5-carat diamond; cursed legend; now in Smithsonian (USA). (3) DARYA-I-NOOR — pink ~182 carats; in Iranian crown jewels. (4) ORLOFF DIAMOND — 189.6 carats; in Russian Imperial Sceptre. (5) REGENT DIAMOND — 140.6 carats; now in Louvre. (6) NIZAM DIAMOND — owned by Nizams of Hyderabad. (7) JACOB DIAMOND — 184.5 carats. KEY: until ~1730 (when Brazilian + later South African mines opened), Golconda was the WORLD'S ONLY KNOWN SOURCE of diamonds. AURANGZEB'S CAMPAIGN: 1687 siege of Golconda Fort (8 months); ABUL HASAN QUTB SHAH (last Qutb Shahi sultan) was imprisoned in Daulatabad. Golconda's wealth funded Mughal coffers briefly. HYDERABAD founded by Quli Qutb Shah (1591). PYQ FREQUENCY: Golconda-diamond link in SSC, UPSC.

questions.explanation: AURANGZEB took the regnal title ALAMGIR — Persian for 'WORLD CONQUEROR' (or 'Conqueror of the Universe'). His full regnal name was MUHI-UD-DIN MUHAMMAD AURANGZEB ALAMGIR PADSHAH GHAZI. KEY TITLES of MUGHAL EMPERORS: (1) BABUR — adopted regnal name BABUR ('the tiger'), simple. (2) HUMAYUN — 'fortunate'. (3) AKBAR — 'great' (by his own designation). (4) JAHANGIR — 'world-seizer' (originally Salim, named after Sheikh Salim Chishti). (5) SHAH JAHAN — 'king of the world' (originally Khurram, after his father). (6) AURANGZEB — 'ALAMGIR' = world conqueror. (7) BAHADUR SHAH — 'brave king'. (8) FARRUKHSIYAR — 'auspicious figure'. (9) MUHAMMAD SHAH — 'praiseworthy king'. (10) BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR — last Mughal, executed/exiled to Burma 1858. AURANGZEB's wars EARNED him 'Alamgir' title — but he never quite conquered the world; Mughals never extended beyond India in his time. The IRONY: 'World Conqueror' title at the very moment Mughal empire began OVEREXTENDING and DECLINING. AURANGZEB IN HISTORICAL DEBATE: most controversial Mughal — destroyed temples (Kashi Vishwanath at Varanasi, Krishna Janmabhoomi at Mathura, Somnath); BUT also pragmatic, generous to many Hindu officials; Marathas had Hindu officers in his army. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'Alamgir' title in UPSC, MPSC, SSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Aurangzeb's grave is located in which city?
questions.explanation: AURANGZEB'S TOMB — located in KHULDABAD (also spelled Khuldābād, formerly Rauza), near the city of AURANGABAD (now SAMBHAJINAGAR after 2022 renaming) in MAHARASHTRA. SIMPLE GRAVE: as per his wishes — small, open-air, made of LIMESTONE; covered with white-marble jali (lattice screen) added later. PHILOSOPHY: Aurangzeb was a DEVOUT MUSLIM in his later years, lived austerely (sewed caps, copied Quran for income — refused royal stipend); his grave reflects this simplicity. CONTRAST with ELABORATE TOMBS: (a) HUMAYUN'S TOMB — Delhi (precursor to Taj). (b) AKBAR'S TOMB — Sikandra, near Agra (mix of styles). (c) JAHANGIR'S TOMB — Shahdara, Lahore (Pakistan). (d) SHAH JAHAN'S TOMB — Taj Mahal, Agra (next to Mumtaz). (e) AURANGZEB's — minimalist, Khuldabad. WHY KHULDABAD: he died in AHMADNAGAR (3 March 1707, age 88) during Deccan campaigns; never returned to north. Khuldabad is a historical Sufi center — site of revered Sufi saints' tombs (e.g., Zar Zari Zar Baksh). NEAR ATTRACTIONS: ELLORA + AJANTA caves (UNESCO Heritage), Daulatabad fort, Bibi-ka-Maqbara (Aurangzeb's son Azam Shah built it — 'mini Taj Mahal' in Aurangabad, 1660-1661). RECENT (2022): Aurangabad city renamed CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR by Maharashtra govt — political move honoring Sambhaji. PYQ FREQUENCY: Aurangzeb tomb location in UPSC, MPSC, SSC 1× per 2 cycles.
